paras.text: 4. Modern technology
paras.urdu: 4۔ جدید ٹیکنالوجی:
paras.pashto: 4. نوې ټکنالوژي

paras.text: Developed countries have, in the past period, taken very great steps forward in technical (i.e. technological) progress, on the basis of which a tremendous increase has occurred in their power to produce goods; but in backward countries only a very small share of modern technology reaches. Backward countries should obtain technology from the outside world, amend it as required according to their particular conditions and requirements, and take steps towards industrial progress. In this connection the example of Japan is worth following. Japan joined the industrial race very late, but at the end of the nineteenth century it, on one side, began sending its students to Western countries to obtain technical training, and on the other side the government created favourable conditions for economic promotion, because of which, moulding foreign technologies according to its own conditions, today Japan has become the second largest industrial country of the world.

paras.text: 5. Provision of social overhead capital (Social Overhead Capital)

paras.text: Political factors (Political Facors)
paras.urdu: سیاسی عوامل: (Political Facors)
paras.pashto: سیاسي عوامل (Political Facors)

paras.text: For the economic progress of any country, along with economic factors, it is also necessary that political factors be favourable. Its meaning is that the government wants to give progress to the country, wants to take it out of the agricultural age and bring it into the age of industrial and atomic energy. The administrative machinery should be efficient and hard-working. In the present age a strong desire for economic progress has arisen in backward countries, and their governments feel their responsibilities in this connection; but in Pakistan political conditions have remained very changeable, turbulent and unstable. For the economic progress of Pakistan it is necessary that the political and administrative machinery be extremely honest, efficient and self-sacrificing. Pakistan is an Islamic republic, but here there are scores of political parties whose manifestos are separate, although the Islamic system of life is a clear, settled, eternal and everlasting reality, and only this manifesto should be desired and present. (Political instability and fragmentation in Pakistan have been discussed in the previous pages.)

په اقتصادي پرمختګ کې ”ټولنیز عوامل“ هم ډېر مهم رول لوبوي. که ټولنیز چاپېریال، تمدني دودونه، ټولنیز رسمونه او نظریې مناسبې وي، د اقتصادي پرمختګ عمل ګړندی وي، که نه سست. که خلک زیارکښ او زغمونکي، با ادبه او لوستي، لرلید او سپمونکي، د سوکاله او پرمختلونکي ژوند هیله‌من وي، نو د اقتصادي پرمختګ لاره پخپله هوارېږي. په وروسته‌پاتې هېوادونو کې ځینې خلک بې‌سواده، ناپوه، خرافاتي، کار تښتونکي، مسلکي سوالګر، ټمبل او اسرافګر وي، او همدا خبرې د هغوی د اقتصادي پرمختګ په لاره کې تر ټولو لوی خنډونه دي.

په پاکستان کې ډېری نفوس بې‌سواده دی، د ساینس او ټکنالوژۍ له نویو غوښتنو ناخبره دی؛ خلک د اقتصادي پرمختګ لپاره د ټولیزې هڅې له شعور بې‌برخې دي؛ اسراف او ښودنې ته عادت دي؛ له زیار او زغم ځان ژغوري. نو تر هغه چې د خلکو … (په ۱۳۹ مخ دوام لري)

4. Modern technology

Developed countries have, in the past period, taken very great steps forward in technical (i.e. technological) progress, on the basis of which a tremendous increase has occurred in their power to produce goods; but in backward countries only a very small share of modern technology reaches. Backward countries should obtain technology from the outside world, amend it as required according to their particular conditions and requirements, and take steps towards industrial progress. In this connection the example of Japan is worth following. Japan joined the industrial race very late, but at the end of the nineteenth century it, on one side, began sending its students to Western countries to obtain technical training, and on the other side the government created favourable conditions for economic promotion, because of which, moulding foreign technologies according to its own conditions, today Japan has become the second largest industrial country of the world.

5. Provision of social overhead capital (Social Overhead Capital)

For industrialisation (Industrialization) and the buying and selling of agricultural produce some initial and basic facilities are needed, e.g. means of transport and communications (e.g. roads, railways, telephone), markets, dams (Dams), irrigation projects, provision of electricity and energy, prevention of epidemic diseases etc. As long as these facilities do not exist, people are not attracted towards investment. As it were, these do the work of external economies (External Economies); therefore these facilities should be provided.

Political factors (Political Facors)

For the economic progress of any country, along with economic factors, it is also necessary that political factors be favourable. Its meaning is that the government wants to give progress to the country, wants to take it out of the agricultural age and bring it into the age of industrial and atomic energy. The administrative machinery should be efficient and hard-working. In the present age a strong desire for economic progress has arisen in backward countries, and their governments feel their responsibilities in this connection; but in Pakistan political conditions have remained very changeable, turbulent and unstable. For the economic progress of Pakistan it is necessary that the political and administrative machinery be extremely honest, efficient and self-sacrificing. Pakistan is an Islamic republic, but here there are scores of political parties whose manifestos are separate, although the Islamic system of life is a clear, settled, eternal and everlasting reality, and only this manifesto should be desired and present. (Political instability and fragmentation in Pakistan have been discussed in the previous pages.)

Social factors (Social Factors)

In economic development “social factors” too play a very important role. If the social environment, civilisational traditions, social customs and theories are favourable, the process of economic development is fast, otherwise slow. If people are hard-working and hardy, cultured and educated, far-sighted and frugal, desirous of passing a prosperous and progressive life, then the path of economic development becomes smooth by itself. In backward countries some people are illiterate, ignorant, superstitious, work-shirkers, professional beggars, lazy and extravagant, and these very things are the biggest obstacles on the path of their economic development.

In Pakistan most of the population is illiterate, unaware of the modern requirements of science and technology; people are deprived of the consciousness of making collective effort for economic progress; they are accustomed to extravagance and display; they shirk labour and hardiness. 4۔ جدید ٹیکنالوجی:

ترقی یافتہ ملکوں نے عرصہ گزشتہ میں، ٹیکنیکی (یعنی فنیاتی) ترقی میں قدم بہت آگے بڑھائے ہیں، جس کی بنا پر ان کی اشیاء پیدا کرنے کی قوت میں بے پناہ اضافہ ہوا ہے، مگر پس ماندہ ملکوں میں جدید ٹیکنالوجی کا صرف معمولی سا حصہ ہی پہنچتا ہے۔ پسماندہ ممالک کو چاہیے کہ بیرونی دنیا سے ٹیکنالوجی حاصل کریں اور اپنے مخصوص حالات اور تقاضوں کے مطابق مطلوبہ ترمیم کر کے، صنعتی ترقی کی جانب قدم بڑھائیں۔ اس سلسلہ میں جاپان کی مثال قابلِ تقلید ہے۔ جاپان صنعتی دوڑ میں بہت بعد میں شامل ہوا تھا لیکن انیسویں صدی کے اواخر میں اس نے ایک طرف اپنے طلبہ کو مغربی ممالک میں فنی تربیت لینے کے لیے بھیجنا شروع کیا اور دوسری طرف حکومت نے معاشی فروغ کے لیے ساز گار حالات پیدا کیے۔ جس کے باعث بیرونی ٹیکنالوجیز کو اپنے حالات کے مطابق ڈھال کر آج جاپان دنیا کا دوسرا سب سے بڑا صنعتی ملک بن چکا ہے۔

5۔ معاشرتی بالائی سرمایہ (Social Overhead Capital) کی بہم رسانی:

صنعت افرازی (Industrialization) اور زرعی پیداوار کی خرید و فروخت کے لیے بعض ابتدائی اور بنیادی سہولتوں کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے، جیسے ذرائع نقل و حمل اور مواصلات (مثلاً سڑکیں، ریلیں، ٹیلی فون)، منڈیاں، بند (Dams)، آبپاشی کے منصوبے، بجلی اور توانائی کی بہم رسانی، وبائی امراض کا انسداد وغیرہ۔ جب تک یہ سہولتیں موجود نہ ہوں، لوگ سرمایہ کاری کی طرف راغب نہیں ہوتے۔ گویا یہ بیرونی کفایات (External Economies) کا کام دیتی ہیں، لہٰذا یہ سہولیات مہیا کی جانی چاہئیں۔

سیاسی عوامل: (Political Facors)

کسی ملک کی معاشی ترقی کے لیے اقتصادی عوامل کے ساتھ ساتھ، سیاسی عوامل کا ساز گار ہونا بھی ضروری ہے، اس کا یہ مطلب ہے کہ حکومت ملک کو ترقی دینا چاہتی ہو، اسے زرعی دور سے نکال کر صنعتی اور جوہری توانائی کے دور میں لانے کی خواہش مند ہو۔ انتظامی مشینری مستعد اور محنتی ہو۔ عہدِ حاضر میں پس ماندہ ممالک میں، معاشی ترقی کی زبردست خواہش پیدا ہوئی ہے، اور ان کی حکومتیں اس سلسلہ میں اپنی ذمہ داریاں محسوس کرتی ہیں، لیکن پاکستان میں سیاسی حالات بڑے تغیر پذیر، ہنگامہ خیز اور غیر مستحکم رہے ہیں۔ پاکستان کی معاشی ترقی کے لیے ضروری ہے کہ سیاسی اور انتظامی مشینری نہایت دیانتدار، مستعد اور ایثار پیشہ ہو۔ پاکستان ایک اسلامی جمہوریہ ہے لیکن یہاں بیسیوں سیاسی جماعتیں ہیں جن کے الگ الگ منشور ہیں حالانکہ اسلامی نظامِ حیات تو ایک واضح، مسلّمہ، دائمی اور ابدی حقیقت ہے اور صرف یہی منشور مطلوب و موجود ہونا چاہیے۔ (پاکستان میں سیاسی عدمِ استحکام اور ٹوٹ پھوٹ پر گزشتہ صفحات میں بحث ہو چکی ہے)

معاشرتی عوامل: (Social Factors)

معاشی ترقی میں ”معاشرتی عوامل“ بھی بڑا اہم کردار ادا کرتے ہیں۔ اگر معاشرتی ماحول، تمدنی روایات، سماجی رسوم و نظریات ساز گار ہوں تو معاشی ترقی کا عمل تیز ہوتا ہے ورنہ سست۔ اگر لوگ محنتی اور جفاکش ہوں، مہذب اور تعلیم یافتہ ہوں، دور اندیش اور کفایت شعار ہوں، خوش حال اور ترقی پذیر زندگی گزارنے کے خواہش مند ہوں، تو معاشی ترقی کا راستہ خود بخود ہموار ہو جاتا ہے۔ پس ماندہ ممالک میں بعض لوگ ان پڑھ، جاہل، اوہام پرست، کام چور، پیشہ ور بھکاری، کاہل اور فضول خرچ ہوتے ہیں، اور یہی باتیں ان کی معاشی ترقی کی راہ میں سب سے بڑی رکاوٹ ہیں۔

پاکستان میں بیشتر آبادی ان پڑھ ہے، سائنس اور ٹیکنالوجی کے جدید تقاضوں سے بے خبر ہے، لوگ معاشی ترقی کے لیے اجتماعی کوشش کرنے کے شعور سے محروم ہیں، فضول خرچی اور نمود و نمائش کے عادی ہیں، محنت اور جفاکشی سے جی چراتے ہیں، اس لیے جب تک لوگوں … (ص 139 پر جاری)

paras.text: In the present age most countries of the world face these problems: poverty, disease, illiteracy, unemployment, agricultural and industrial backwardness, low standard of living, unequal distribution of wealth, dearness and expensiveness, inflation, imbalance in foreign payments, the burden of foreign debt, deficit in the budget etc.
paras.urdu: عہدِ حاضر میں دنیا کے بیشتر ممالک ان مسائل سے دوچار ہیں: غربت، بیماری، ناخواندگی، بے روزگاری، زرعی و صنعتی پس ماندگی، پست معیارِ زندگی، غیر مساوی تقسیمِ دولت، گرانی و مہنگائی، افراطِ زر، بیرونی ادائیگیوں میں عدمِ توازن، غیر ملکی قرضہ کا بوجھ، بجٹ میں خسارہ وغیرہ۔
paras.pashto: په اوسني عصر کې د نړۍ ډېری هېوادونه له دې ستونزو سره مخ دي: بېوزلي، ناروغي، بې‌سوادي، بې‌روزګاري، کرنیز او صنعتي وروسته‌پاتې والی، د ژوند ټیټ معیار، د شتمنۍ نابرابر وېش، ګراني، انفلاسیون، په بهرنیو تادیو کې عدم توازن، د بهرني پور بار، په بودجه کې زیان او نور.

paras.text: Although the existence of poverty and want is from the ancient age, the desire to get rid of it, and the hope that it can be got rid of, are the product of the present age, because not only has, by virtue of the progress of science and technology, the better use of resources become possible, but the concept of economic planning too has become very popular, and some nations have made enviable progress by virtue of economic planning.
paras.urdu: اگرچہ غربت و افلاس کا وجود عہدِ قدیم سے ہے لیکن اس سے چھٹکارا پانے کی خواہش اور یہ امید کہ چھٹکارا پایا جا سکتا ہے، زمانہ حال کی پیداوار ہیں، کیونکہ نہ صرف سائنس و ٹیکنالوجی کی ترقی کی بدولت وسائل کا بہتر استعمال ممکن ہو گیا ہے، بلکہ معاشی منصوبہ بندی کا تصور بھی بہت مقبول ہو گیا ہے اور بعض اقوام نے معاشی منصوبہ بندی کی بدولت قابلِ رشک ترقی کی ہے۔
paras.pashto: که څه هم د بېوزلۍ او غربت شتون له پخوانۍ دورې دی، خو له هغې د خلاصون هیله او دا هیله چې خلاصون شونی دی، د اوسني عصر محصول دي؛ ځکه نه یوازې د ساینس او ټکنالوژۍ د پرمختګ په برکت د سرچینو ښه کارونه شونې شوې، بلکې د اقتصادي پلان جوړونې مفهوم هم ډېر مشهور شوی، او ځینو ملتونو د اقتصادي پلان جوړونې په برکت د رشک وړ پرمختګ کړی دی.

paras.text: Definition of economic planning (Defination of Economic Planning)
paras.urdu: معاشی منصوبہ بندی کی تعریف: (Defination of Economic Planning)
paras.pashto: د اقتصادي پلان جوړونې تعریف (Defination of Economic Planning)

Economic planning (Economic Planning)

Concept of economic planning (Concept of Economic Planning)

In the present age most countries of the world face these problems: poverty, disease, illiteracy, unemployment, agricultural and industrial backwardness, low standard of living, unequal distribution of wealth, dearness and expensiveness, inflation, imbalance in foreign payments, the burden of foreign debt, deficit in the budget etc.

Although the existence of poverty and want is from the ancient age, the desire to get rid of it, and the hope that it can be got rid of, are the product of the present age, because not only has, by virtue of the progress of science and technology, the better use of resources become possible, but the concept of economic planning too has become very popular, and some nations have made enviable progress by virtue of economic planning.

Definition of economic planning (Defination of Economic Planning)

Different economists have defined economic planning in different ways. For example, Professor Lewis Lorwin (Lewis Larwin) writes: “By economic planning is meant such an arrangement of economic organisation in which different factories, business organisations and industries are conceived as mutually helpful units of one single system, so that in a fixed period, utilising all existing means and resources, the needs of people are fulfilled in the best way.”

Professor Dickinson (Dickenson), in his book “Economics of Socialism”, defines planning in these words: “By economic planning are meant some big decisions of the authority and responsible body of a country, e.g. which goods should be produced, in what quantity they should be made and for whom they should be made; these decisions are made after taking a complete review of the whole economic system.”

In short, in economic planning three things have central position:

First, determining objectives (Objectives) by using reason and wisdom.

Second, bringing all resources of the country into use in such a way that the desired objectives are achieved.

Third, establishing a responsible authority, which has central powers, to give the plan practical shape.

(continued from p.138) … outlook of life of people, they will not be able to fulfil the social requirements of the modern age.

Education plays a very important role in making social factors favourable; therefore for economic progress there is need of such a system of education which:

• helps our economy in entering the age of science and technology;

• proves helpful in political, social and economic progress;

• raises the educational standard so that the youth of the nation can discharge national responsibilities properly.

Economic planning (Economic Planning)

Concept of economic planning (Concept of Economic Planning)

In the present age most countries of the world face these problems: poverty, disease, illiteracy, unemployment, agricultural and industrial backwardness, low standard of living, unequal distribution of wealth, dearness and expensiveness, inflation, imbalance in foreign payments, the burden of foreign debt, deficit in the budget etc.

Although the existence of poverty and want is from the ancient age, the desire to get rid of it, and the hope that it can be got rid of, are the product of the present age, because not only has, by virtue of the progress of science and technology, the better use of resources become possible, but the concept of economic planning too has become very popular, and some nations have made enviable progress by virtue of economic planning.

Definition of economic planning (Defination of Economic Planning)

Different economists have defined economic planning in different ways. For example, Professor Lewis Lorwin (Lewis Larwin) writes: “By economic planning is meant such an arrangement of economic organisation in which different factories, business organisations and industries are conceived as mutually helpful units of one single system, so that in a fixed period, utilising all existing means and resources, the needs of people are fulfilled in the best way.”

Professor Dickinson (Dickenson), in his book “Economics of Socialism”, defines planning in these words: “By economic planning are meant some big decisions of the authority and responsible body of a country, e.g. which goods should be produced, in what quantity they should be made and for whom they should be made; these decisions are made after taking a complete review of the whole economic system.”

In short, in economic planning three things have central position:

First, determining objectives (Objectives) by using reason and wisdom.

Second, bringing all resources of the country into use in such a way that the desired objectives are achieved.

Third, establishing a responsible authority, which has central powers, to give the plan practical shape.

Need and importance of planning in Pakistan (Need of Economic Planning in Pakistan)

Pakistan is a backward (Backward) and developing (Developing) country. It faces different problems, e.g. low national production, low per capita income, over-population, inflation, shortage of technical information, the bad balance of payments, the burden of foreign loans, little use of machines in agriculture, unfavourable terms of trade, unemployment, defective system of distribution of wealth etc. The remedy for all these problems is … (continued on p.140)
